newsitem.title: CANADA: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO LEADS AT CANADIAN CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-STOJKO LEADS AT CANADIAN CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: As expected, Elvis Stojko blew away the competition Friday in the short programme at the Bank of Montreal Canadian Figure Skating Championships before 14,500 appreciative fans.

The 24-year-old whose steely nerves earned him the nickname "The Terminator" scored 5.8s and 5.9s for the required jumps, spins and footwork sequences and 5.8s for presentation. The best his closest of 15 challengers could manage were 5.5s and 5.6s out of the perfect score of 6.0.
Skating to the soundtrack from the movie "The Rocketeer," Stojko executed each element, including a triple Axel-double toe combo, with machine-like precision.
"I'm excited about doing the quad" in Saturday's final, said Stojko. "The audience, everyone gets hyped about that."

The two-time Canadian and world champion plans to turn up the heat -- and the difficulty of his short programme -- at the Champions Series Final later this month and world championship in March. "For the next two competitions, I'll bump it up to a triple-triple and go from there," said Stojko.

"My programmes have been getting really good reviews this year and the artistic marks have been up there with the technical," said Stojko, whose decidedly non-classical approach to the sport has sometimes gone unrewarded by international judging panels.

"The Champions Series and worlds are right around the corner," said Stojko's long-time coach Doug Leigh, who also took Canadian Brian Orser to the top of the world in 1987. "We've done a lot of work but we have to keep the process going.
He added: "(Russians) Kulik and Urmanov and (American) Todd (Eldredge) aren't here. There's lots coming yet. You have to keep the big picture in focus."
Jeff Langdon, Stojko's training mate at the Mariposa School north of Toronto, was second while Stephane Yvars from the province of Quebec scored third place marks.
